author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this insightful talk, Dr. Prafull Prabhakar Gadge, Founder, CEO, and Principal Scientist at Biome Technologies, explains why the future of food, farming, and human health depends on something most of us never think about—microorganisms in soil.

While conversations about soil degradation often focus on fertilizers and chemicals, Dr. Gadge reveals a deeper issue: the loss of microbial life in soil. These microscopic organisms act as the biological engine that helps plants absorb nutrients, resist diseases, and adapt to environmental stress.

Through his groundbreaking innovation, Soilometer, Dr. Gadge developed a practical way for farmers to quickly measure soil microbial health—making advanced soil diagnostics accessible and affordable. By helping farmers understand and restore the living ecosystem beneath their feet, this technology has enabled many to reduce chemical use, improve crop quality, and significantly increase income.

He shares inspiring real-world examples of farmers
title: Soil Microbes: The Invisible Engine of Life | Dr. Prafull Prabhakar Gadge | TEDxDCAC

In this talk, Ciaran Mullooly argues that true inclusion requires a shift in mindset: accessibility must become a habit embedded in how we design spaces, services and communities. Drawing on the work of the Lough Ree, Access for All project, he explores how small changes in thinking can create a society where everyone can participate fully. Ciaran Mullooly is an MEP for Midlands–North-West and a former RTÉ journalist with 26 years’ experience.
